settings.name_in_paper: High-dimensional kernelized (nonparametric) contextual bandit with K arms (no-regret regime)
unmapped: Each of the K arms has its own d-dimensional context X^(i)(t), i.i.d. over rounds but possibly correlated across arms, and its own unknown reward function f^(i) in the RKHS with norm <= B
Dimension d grows with T (high-dimensional asymptotic regime d = Theta(T^tau_1))
Whitened contexts have independent, bounded, zero-mean unit-variance coordinates; covariance operator norm <= 1
Kernel with 1/d scaling (inner-product or RBF class), K(x,x) <= 1
Noise has zero mean and variance <= sigma^2 (no sub-Gaussianity)
settings.definition_quote: The forecaster chooses an arm $\Ich \in [K]$ based on the $\Xit$ values of all the arms, and then observes a reward ... $\Yt = f_\ast^{(I(t))}( \Xt) + \xi(t)$ ... The independent noise term $\xi(t)$ has zero mean and bounded variance $\Var[\xi(t)] \leq \sigma^2$ ... A reward function $f_\ast^{(i)}$ is an element of RKHS $\mH$ and satisfies norm $\|f_\ast^{(i)}\|_\mH \leq B$

settings.name_in_paper: High-dimensional kernelized contextual bandit, lenient regret (non-vanishing generalization error regime)
unmapped: Per-arm contexts and per-arm RKHS reward functions with norm <= B
Regret is lenient: per-round regret below a tolerance Delta_len is not counted
The learner knows the lenient tolerance Delta_len, the covariance-structure parameter eps and kernel quantities (h'', h') used to set the exploration length T0
settings.definition_quote: $R_{\Delta}(T) = \sum_{t=1}^T \Phi_{\Delta}\rbr{r(t)}$, where $\Phi_{\Delta}(a) = \max\{a - \Delta, 0\}$, and $\Delta > 0$ is the hyperparameter specified before the algorithm run.

symbols.tau_2: exponent with eps = Theta(T^-tau_2), tau_2 in (0, tau_1/4)

conditions: kernel from the inner-product class with 1/d scaling, K(x,x) <= 1
Assumption 4.1 (RKHS norm <= B, ||Sigma||_op <= 1, whitened contexts with independent bounded coordinates)
d = Theta(T^tau_1), tau_1 in (0,1)
low-rank covariance (Case I): Sigma = diag(1,...,1,0,...,0) with rank eps*d, eps = Theta(T^-tau_2), tau_2 in (0, tau_1/4)

source.label: thm:etc_reg_simple
source.quote: Consider a kernel from the inner-product class as Definition \ref{def:kernel_class}. Suppose that $d = \Theta(T^{\tau_1})$ and Assumption~\ref{asmp:basic} holds, where $\tau_1 \in (0, 1)$. Furthermore, assume the contexts are generated through low-rank covariance structure (Case I in \exref{ex:liang_sec4}) with $\varepsilon = \Theta(T^{-\tau_2})$, where $\tau_2 \in (0, \tau_1 / 4)$. Then, with $\overline{\tau} = \min\cbr{{\tau_1}/  {2}, \tau_2, \tau_1 - 4\tau_2} > 0$, EtC with the exploration duration $T_0 = \Theta(Kd)$ is a no-regret algorithm, and the regret satisfies $R(T) = \tilde{O}\rbr{T^{\max\{\tau_1, 1 - {\overline{\tau}}/  {2}\}}}$.

results.notes: Regret defined via expected f values versus per-round optimal arm, so pseudo-regret against best action per round. Exploration length depends on d, not T; horizon marked anytime, though the asymptotic regime ties d to T. Noise only has bounded variance.

Assumption 4.1
d = Theta(T^tau_1), tau_1 in (0,1)
||X_1^(i)|| = o(d^-c) and gamma_d^(i) >= c_underline Tr(Sigma)/d for sufficiently large d and some c > 0
low-rank covariance (Case I) with eps = Theta(T^-tau_2), tau_2 in (0, tau_1/2)

source.label: thm:etc_reg_simple_rbf
source.quote: Consider a kernel from the RBF class as Definition \ref{def:kernel_class}. Suppose that $d = \Theta(T^{\tau_1})$ and Assumption~\ref{asmp:basic} holds, where $\tau_1 \in (0, 1)$. Also, suppose that $\|X_1^{(i)}\| = o(d^{-c})$ and $\gamma_d^{(i)} \geq \underline{c} \mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma_d^{(i)})/d$ hold ... with $\varepsilon = \Theta(T^{-\tau_2})$, where $\tau_2 \in (0, \tau_1 / 2)$. Then, with $\overline{\tau} = \min\cbr{{\tau_1}/  {2}, \tau_2, \tau_1 - 2\tau_2} > 0$, EtC with the exploration duration $T_0 = \Theta(Kd)$ is a no-regret algorithm, and the regret satisfies $R(T) = \tilde{O}(T^{\max\cbr{\tau_1, 1-2\tau_1, 1- c\tau_1, 1 - {\overline{\tau}} / {2}}})$.

conditions: quantity is lenient regret R_Delta(T) = sum_t max(r(t) - Delta_len, 0)
kernel from the inner-product class
setup of Theorem 4.6 (c_L <= d/N <= c_U, Assumption 4.1)
covariance of Case I, II or III of Example 1
d = Theta(T^tau), tau in (0,1)
eps sufficiently small as a function of Delta_len (e.g. Case I: 3B^2 h''_max eps^2/4 + B^2 beta eps < Delta_len/(4K))
tuning: T0 = O(d); e.g. Case I and II: T0 = ceil(256 sigma^2 K^2 eps / Delta_len) d; Case III: T0 = floor(eps^2 h''_min Delta_len/(64 sigma^2 beta)) d

source.label: thm:etc_lr_Td
source.quote: Fix any $\Delta > 0$ as a constant. Consider the setup of Theorem \ref{thm:inner-product} with the cases $\mathrm{I}$, $\mathrm{II}$, and $\mathrm{III}$ as Example \ref{ex:liang_sec4}. ... assume that $d = \Theta(T^{\tau})$ holds for some $\tau \in (0, 1)$. Furthermore, each of the cases $\mathrm{I}$, $\mathrm{II}$, and $\mathrm{III}$, if $\varepsilon$ is sufficiently small as a function of $\Delta$, then we can choose $T_0 = O(d)$ and the lenient regret for each of the three examples in Example \ref{ex:liang_sec4} is $R_{\Delta}(T) = O(d) = o(T)$.

results.notes: Lenient regret (not standard regret); quantity 'other'. The Delta here is the lenient tolerance, not an arm gap. Exploration length per Table 2 in the appendix.

source.quote: Fix any $\Delta > 0$. Suppose that Assumption~\ref{asmp:basic} holds and $\varepsilon > 0$ is constant. Furthermore, assume that $d = \Theta(T^{\tau})$ holds for some $\tau \in (0, 1)$. Then, the lenient regret for each of the three examples in Example \ref{ex:liang_sec4} is $R_{\Delta}(T) = O(T^\tau)$ if $\varepsilon$ is small enough such that $-5B^2 h_{\mathrm{min}}' \varepsilon < \frac{\Delta}{4K}$ ...

results.notes: Lenient regret for the RBF class; O(T^tau) = O(d).
